title: Gas Bill Tracking Seasonal Usage Baseline
dataSources: Utility bills (`utility:bill`), utility meter readings (`utility:meter`), utility rate changes (`utility:rate`), household accounts (`household:account`), utility payments (`utility:payment`).
app: Electric, gas, and water bills, smart-meter readings, household-account records, and utility rate-plan changes streamed to Splunk HEC via portals, CSV exports, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=utility:bill bill_type="gas"
| stats avg(usage_therms) as avg_usage by season
| eventstats avg(avg_usage) as overall_usage
| eval delta=round(avg_usage-overall_usage,2)
| sort - delta
description: Shows how the usage behind gas bill tracking shifts by season compared with the annual average.
value: Seasonal baselines tell you whether a bill spike is expected weather behavior or a true anomaly worth investigating.
implementation: Populate a simple season field during ingest so the chart stays readable.
visualization: Bar chart of seasonal average usage versus overall average.
grandmaExplanation: It measures whether one season regularly makes gas bill tracking much heavier or lighter than normal.
